children: Power and grid-equipment manufacturer GE Vernova

is extending its digital-twin capabilities across power systems and AI factories, aligning with NVIDIA's DSX architecture. Shares fell 10.43% to $829.31 at 11:25 a.m. ET Thursday. The collaboration targets a costly problem: coordinating electricity supply and computing demand before construction begins. NVIDIA announced the initiative in March, so it does not establish a fresh explanation for Thursday's selloff.

The demand story still has muscle. GE Vernova reported a $176 billion backlog at the end of the second quarter, with data-center orders exceeding $5 billion in the first halfmore than twice its full-year 2025 total. But orders are only the starting line. According to Reuters' second-quarter coverage, widening Wind losses weighed on results despite growth in Power and Electrification. Turning demand into profitable deliveries remains the test.

The valuation snapshot shows a 23.74 price-to-earnings ratio alongside a GF Score of just 17/100, a reminder that one earnings multiple cannot capture the full investment picture. Digital twins could help customers catch design problems earlier. They cannot manufacture turbines, deliver transformers or secure grid connections by themselves. For investors, the next proof point is execution: converting that enormous backlog into revenue, cash and stronger margins.

title: GE Vernova Stocks Slide 10.43% as AI-Power Modeling Deepens
